#968. Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors

The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

With just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant. This comes after the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had said it had been removed from the tournament so that Russia could take part.

The move, which has yet to be publicly announced by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play. The World Juniors is the first tournament affected by the CAS decision.

The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a statement issued Saturday, the IIHF said it was "taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey."

As of Monday, the IIHF website still listed Norway as one of the participants in the World Juniors, which is to be hosted by Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta, beginning on December 26. But Swiss Ice Hockey has responded to Norway's statement, saying its team would not face Russia at the World Juniors — as would be the case if it replaces Norway in the schedule.

However, it's far from certain that Russia will actually be able to ice a team in the tournament, as just last week, the Canadian prime minister ruled out the possibility.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," said Mark Carney.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there."

How this circle could be squared is unclear. Carney's pledge, coupled with the stated refusal by Finland, Sweden, Switzerland and others to face Russia in an international tournament, appears to have given the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association (NIHF) hope that its team could still play in the upcoming tournament. Several long-time corporate sponsors have also threatened to pull out if Russia is allowed to compete.

"This makes us hope that the last word has not been said about our participation in Canada in December," said NIHF General Secretary Petter Salsten.

"The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association is awaiting further information from the IIHF in the coming days."

Meanwhile, the German Ice Hockey Association (DEB) is still in discussions with the government in Berlin and the IIHF about how to proceed — or not — with hosting the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in May.

"We intend to host the world championship in Germany next year, and I am very optimistic that we will succeed in doing so," DEB chairman Frank H. Lutz told German broadcaster MagentaSport on Saturday.

While he acknowledged the IIHF's CAS-ordered requirement to include Russia and reiterated the DEB's rejection of the court ruling, he provided no indication as to how this obstacle could be overcome.

Lutz, who said he would be in Berlin for more consultations this week, had previously said handing back Germany's hosting rights was a possibility — if only as a last resort.

On Friday, government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said Berlin supports the DEB's efforts to find a solution.

"However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore, through dialogue, how we can still ensure the tournament takes place."

Asked at the same press conference whether Germany could issue visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman indicated that this would be difficult under restrictions currently in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," said spokesperson Martin Giese.

However, he did not categorically rule out the possibility.

It has been suggested that government officials could be choosing their words carefully out of concern for Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees who are bidding to host an Olympic Games — like the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) — to follow its lead.

Asked whether the debate over Russia's possible involvement in a hockey tournament could affect Munich's chances, government spokesman Kornelius said he didn't wish to "speculate on implications."

Still, with the IOC set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process, one has to think that the issue could hardly have come up at a more inopportune time for the DOSB.

#967. England stun world champions Spain in one of their greatest victories

Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

Trafford again! 👊🏻 An excellent double save from the Leeds United keeper 🙌 https://t.co/L27oQFQO1J

This was a performance good enough to win a World Cup final, never mind Nations League Group A3 – just a shame England neglected to get to that World Cup final in the summer. The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabián Ruiz first tangled and others dived in.

There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

Harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

Only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

The defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England showed on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel said, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

They all had their moments. Anthony Gordon had a strong first half. Morgan Rogers was central to the two goals England scored in the 10 minutes after the break. Anderson demonstrated that he is one of the best midfielders in the world in the hour before his red card. Spain were without Rodri and in his absence his Manchester City successor was in control.

Tuchel encouraged his players to mount a ferocious press against the best first-phase passing team in the world. Brave, but it worked beautifully and for an absorbing opening 10 minutes, Spain looked all at sea. Such was the pressure, the Spain goalkeeper Unai Simón abandoned the usual build-up strategy and launched his goal-kicks to the halfway line.

Even when Spain finally found their rhythm at the mid-point of the first half, England adapted. It took them a while to manage the discomfort of being denied the ball, and the familiar rapid incursions and switches of play. The counter-attacking switch from the early period pressing Spain in their own area yielded the penalty from which Kane scored the first.

Anderson snapped into Marc Cucurella and played in Kane with a straight pass punched through the Spain lines. With all his cunning, Kane knew that he could not out-sprint Pau Cubarsi, but he could sucker him into a foul which the England captain did expertly before dispatching the penalty.

It was only another Jarell Quansah error that got Spain back into the game. His mistake allowed Fermin López to play in Yamal for the run in which he was fouled by Anderson for the red card and the subsequent penalty.

Quansah is trying to do the hardest thing asked of a centre-half: play the ball out from the back. His red card in Mexico City and his mistake on Thursday against Croatia have not helped. Thomas Tuchel praised England’s “statement win” that ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run and secured top spot ahead of the world champions in the Nations League.

Tuchel and Declan Rice revealed they had both believed England would end Spain’s long unbeaten streak, and their confidence proved well-founded.

“This was of course a statement victory,” Tuchel said. “I’m happy the players felt so confident. I felt it as well. I also had the same belief [that England would win]. I think we felt it from each other.

“The result followed the performance. I think it was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, in all aspects of the game.”

Tuchel described the nature of England’s win as “the Azteca reloaded” in reference to the World Cup victory over Mexico, but felt the win in Madrid was the best of his reign as head coach.

He said: “Yeah [it was the best performance of his reign so far], given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. They were unbeaten in 43 games. So putting a performance out there in Madrid, in this environment, that was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

“The last half an hour felt like Azteca reloaded, to be honest. Again, it was a beautiful week. The commitment to get better is on the highest level.

“I said it many times, I love these players and I love the mentality .We’re building something and that was the next step. It was an amazing atmosphere. I will bottle it up for sure and then unfortunately we have to wait until the quarter-final.”

Asked what beating Spain can do for England’s belief, before the draw for the quarter-finals of the Nations League on Friday, Tuchel said: “You want confidence, not only through results, but confidence through performance and the result follows.

“That’s the ideal process and that’s what we got. We got it through the whole campaign of the Nations League, we trusted the process and improved our game and took steps forward match by match.

“We had a fantastic result and performance in Croatia followed up by a very good performance at home against Czechia. We then got our homework done against Croatia three days ago and that’s what we always wanted.

“We wanted to come back and compete on the highest level and see how far we can push our limits and how far we can push the opponent with the way we want to play and stay true to our identity. The team did excellent.”

England survived a Spanish fightback to round off their Nations League group-stage campaign in style with a 3-2 win over the world champions in Madrid.

Thomas Tuchel will speak openly to England’s players about what they should do if they encounter racism in the Nations League Group 3 decider with Spain.

This is the first time England have faced Spain in Madrid since November 2004 when they were beaten 1-0 in the Santiago Bernabéu, a game that was ravaged by obscene chanting. The nations were supposed to play a fixture in the Spanish capital in 2008, but the Football Association insisted it be moved to Seville instead.

Earlier this year, Spanish supporters brought shame on themselves again after a flurry of anti-Muslim chants marred a friendly against Egypt; they were fined $20,000 by Fifa and must play their next friendly in a partially closed stadium.

There will be a full house in the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday night, as the reigning world and European champions aim to defend their extraordinary unbeaten run of 43 games, and England head coach Tuchel is adamant the atmosphere will be in keeping with the occasion.

The German has, however, made it clear he and his staff will use their platform before the contest to remind England’s players of the steps they should take if the worst scenario unfolds.

Asked about incidents that had pockmarked this fixture before, Tuchel said: “I think I hear it the first time that this happens. I think it’s unacceptable. In any stadium, not even in stadiums, we will never accept racism. We will never be racist towards anyone.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of England’s final Nations League Group 3 decider as Thomas Tuchel’s side take on Spain at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

Although both countries are safely through to the quarter-finals, England will seek revenge on Spain, who beat them in the Euro 2024 final and in their previous Nations League face-off on September 26 at Wembley. That day, Luis de la Fuente’s men profited from Harry Kane’s uncharacteristic penalty miss, England’s general wastefulness in front of goal and some seriously lacklustre defending to earn a chaotic 3-2 comeback victory after falling 2-1 behind at half-time.

Since that defeat, England have won four successive Nations League fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia by an aggregate score of 14-1. Last time out, they beat Croatia on Thursday, earning a 2-1 win as Kane, who became England’s most-capped men’s player with 126 appearances, dispatched a second-half penalty to seal the three points. Spearheaded by the Ballon d’Or holder’s brilliance, England must win this evening in order to overtake Spain and top the group.

🇪🇸 ALL SET FOR TONIGHT'S BIG SHOWDOWN! 🔥 The Spanish flag is flying high over the Metropolitano, ready to welcome both teams and all the fans for a night of football to remember. ❤️ #VamosEspaña | #NationsLeague https://t.co/EClJMbjxfj

Speaking ahead of the match, Tuchel said: “I think we are ready to win. Now it’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength. I think that’s what we want to see. And then you can never predict the result in football, never. But it’s important that we show the mindset that you speak of and the spirit, and we will. I’m very confident about that.”

Meanwhile, fresh from lifting the World Cup in the summer, Spain have a 100% winning record in this season’s Nations League. They currently boast a staggering 43-match unbeaten run in all competitions, since losing a friendly to Colombia back in March 2024. England’s task is daunting, but not impossible.

Kick-off is at 19:45, with team news coming shortly.

#966. How to become a football referee

Honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done. You find so much more out about yourself that you probably never knew.

Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.

What does a women's referee pathway officer do?

Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.

What kind of training do you give to aspiring referees?

So from going through recruitment courses first of all, and then we do the beginners course with referees, just giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge, then we will also do a practical part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we'll go through scenarios, positioning, things around free kick management for example, other set pieces likecorners, penalty setup, what you do as a referee day to day, even pre match stuff as well, so when you arrive at the grounds, how you check the pitch, check all the equipment is there, how you would interact with players, coaches and then just again, maybe createlike a role play sort of environment so that they know that they're not going totally blind into that sort of situation.

Have you always been passionate about football?

Football was a passion of mine, even when I was younger, primary school age, we just didn't have very many female teams, so it normally meant playing with the boys and the boys teams and stuff up until I was about 14, which was the minimum age here you can join senior ladies football team, which is what I did, and played there for 14 years at a club here locally, including up until the Women's Premiership, so it was great to be involved in football, but I always loved watching football, playing football, anything to do with football, I was always there and interested.

How did you go from playing football to being a referee?

Becoming a referee for me sort of happened by chance to be honest. It was during a game, one time I got an injury, quite a bad injury to my knee and then I had seen luckily that the referee course was being advertised. So I signed up for it, but I also signed up for a coaching course pretty much at the same time, maybe about six weeks apart. I wasnât really sure which role I wanted to follow, but over that winter I had been pushed into refereeing a wee bit and said sure, why not, Iâll give it a go, it'd be a bit of extra fitness before my season restarts, and then just fell in love with it from there and never looked back.

What subjects did you study at school and university?

Coming through school I always picked PE, so I did my GCSE PE and then I also did A-level PE and then when I went onto university,I had the sport and exercise science as well within that, so I think it gives you a good understanding of obviously how your body works, and your plan and training, stuff like that as well so you know when you're working nutrition wise, things that you need to know,especially as you reach the top level, just to make sure that you're getting the most out of your body.

What are your top tips for becoming a referee?

I would say definitely give it a try for sure. You never know until you do it. I think even when I was a player, I probably never imaginedthat I would be a referee and that I would even achieve and have experienced what Iâve been able to experience. So you never knowuntil you give it a go, but it's also about probably pushing yourself out of your comfort zone, being comfortable with being uncomfortable in situations like that. It's maybe not always as bad as it probably seems it's going to be. There's probably a lot more stigma around being a referee - who wants to be a referee? - but honestly for me, it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.

With a lifelong love of football, Louise Thompson followed her passion for the game, first as a player and now as a referee. As well as refereeing Fifa and NIFL Premiership matches, she also works for the Irish Football Association as the women's referee pathway officer, recruiting and developing up-and-coming female refs.

Louise Thompson on refereeing the Women's Irish Cup final.

If you're interested in becoming a referee, it's something you can get involved with from a young age through local referee courses. The minimum age to become a qualified referee varies depending on where in the UK you live:

In her role as a women's referee pathway officer, Louise oversees new referees right from the initial recruitment courses stage: "We then do the beginners' course with referees, giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge," she says. "We also do a hands-on part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we go through different scenariosâ¦ exactly what you do as a referee, and day-to-day practical stuff as wellâ¦ The idea is to give them all the basics and fundamentals before they go into a game so that they're prepared."

All four UK nations have established pathways for referee development and progression. Starting out at grassroots level, it's possible to progress all the way to Fifa!

Louise's first games were youth games: "I still remember my first game to this day," she says. "It was an under-13 game, and I was definitely the most nervous person on the pitch." She explains: "Over time, you'll get mentors who will come and watch you, give you advice, give you feedback" which will help you to progress to higher levels of the game.

As well as PE, Louise has found that languages are really helpful in this line of work, "especially when you're dealing with a lot of international games and people coming along," she says. "If you can learn some languages, it's very, very useful."

You could get into this role by training with a professional body.

Sources: National Careers Service, GOV.UK, FA, IFA, SFA, and FAW.

#965. How Emile Heskey fell into a sketchy world peddling controversial drugs: From England star worth £12m to bankruptcy, unpaid tax and a bitter divorce

Published: 07:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 26 November 2026

Emile Heskey is standing in a warehouse, dressed in a black adidas tracksuit, trying to sell you a jar of curious sweet treats.

He smiles into the camera with the gentle-giant warmth that characterised his football career – but Heskey is in unfamiliar territory.

Behind him, stacked on shelf after shelf, are containers full of Supreme CBD gummies.

The man who scored in England's 5-1 thrashing of Germany in 2001, who scored 110 Premier League goals for Leicester, Liverpool, Birmingham, Wigan and Aston Villa plus seven more for his country, is, remarkably, trying to flog you an assortment of products containing cannabidiol, a legal but controversial ingredient derived from cannabis.

Today, he is promoting a tub of CBD strawberry gummies, as well as oil. If you fancy an exclusive discount, there's a special code bearing his name.

‘I swear by these products for my sleep,’ he writes in the caption on Instagram. ‘They have been fantastic for me for years now!’

Emile Heskey spends his days trying to flog controversial Supreme CBD products (Instagram: theemileheskey)

He is one of multiple former footballers promoting the products for ex-Olympic boxer Anthony Fowler - despite their illegal claims about the supposed health benefits

Heskey, 48, was once one of English football's most respected players. He won 62 caps for England, appearing at two World Cups. He won five trophies at Liverpool and two League Cups at Leicester.

Occasionally mocked for his lack of goals – he averaged roughly one every five games during his club career – he carried himself with humour and grace. Since retiring, his reputation has helped him secure roles with England's youth pathway and Leicester's women's team, as well as occasional punditry work for the BBC.

In September, he scored in an England legends match against Poland, playing alongside John Terry and Robbie Fowler. This month, he was a guest of honour at Liverpool's Anfield VIP Experience. He remains a regular on the speakers' circuit, with more appearances booked before Christmas.

All of which begs the question: what is he doing promoting Supreme CBD? Why is he filming several videos a month for a company with such a troubled regulatory record?

Where once he shared a dressing room with Steven Gerrard and David Beckham, he now shares an ambassadorial roster with Katie Price.

It is unclear whether Heskey is aware of the concerns surrounding Supreme CBD products, or the repeated occasions on which the company has fallen foul of advertising rules.

Its founder, Anthony Fowler, a former Team GB Olympic boxer, has made unsubstantiated claims that his cannabidiol products can help treat mental health conditions and autism in children.

There is likely a financial incentive for Heskey, although the terms of any arrangement are unclear. Equally, he appears genuinely convinced of the products' benefits. He claims the oil has done wonders for his sleep and eased his aches and pains.

Heskey's wife Chantelle has issued divorce proceedings - and claims he cancelled a holiday with their kids to go away with his new partner instead

Heskey and his new partner Jade Slusarczyk spent two weeks together in Cyprus and Greece

Chantelle branded Heskey 'vile' and claimed he deleted her comment on an Instagram post about the new couple's holiday

That may well be true. The NHS acknowledges that CBD has some medical uses, but warns that the ‘quality and content’ of products sold online can be uncertain and that they ‘may be illegal and potentially dangerous’. Nor is there any guarantee that products sold in health stores will be of ‘good quality’.

Supreme CBD have repeatedly breached advertising rules. In June, the Advertising Standards Authority took action over the company's continued use of prohibited claims that CBD could treat, prevent or cure human disease.

The regulator has also upheld complaints about celebrity promotions that failed to make clear they were advertisements.

Supreme CBD have made claims that their products can treat anxiety, insomnia and depression. Such medicinal claims are prohibited in advertising for products that have not been authorised as medicines. It is uncomfortable ground for Heskey to find himself on.

Last year, Fowler also spoke about refusing chemotherapy for his two-year-old daughter's tumour, claiming CBD oil had had a 'massive' effect on it instead. Price, a paid brand ambassador, amplified those claims on her own social media channels, including posted to her 1.6million followers on X that the tumour had 'shrunk' as a result.

British medical and food safety authorities advise that CBD should not be given to those under the age of 18.

CBD can also affect how other medicines work, meaning anyone using it alongside other treatments should seek medical advice. Certain medicinal CBD treatments require regular monitoring because of their potential effects on the liver.

It is not unusual for former sportspeople to struggle with insomnia, depression or persistent pain after retirement. In a digital world where anyone can extol the virtues of a product to thousands of followers, it is perhaps unsurprising that cannabis oil has attracted so much attention. Some users say it has helped them.

Heskey celebrates with David Beckham after scoring for England against Denmark at the 2002 World Cup

Many of Heskey's almost 100,000 Instagram followers appear equally enthusiastic, with comments beneath his posts endorsing the benefits he describes.

And Heskey is hardly alone among former footballers. Supreme CBD products have also been endorsed by former Arsenal and England playmaker Paul Merson – who has his name on a bundle of his 'favourite' products available to buy on the company's website – Heskey's old Liverpool team-mate Chris Kirkland, Southampton hero Matt Le Tissier and ex-Nottingham Forest goalkeeper Mark Crossley, while ex-Liverpool striker John Aldridge has insisted the product was ‘good for me’.

Life after football has, at times, been rather messy for Heskey.

In 2009, his wealth was estimated at £12million. He had built a clean-cut image and maintained a relatively low profile away from the pitch. Yet just a year later, in 2010, he was declared bankrupt.

His subsequent business dealings have brought further difficulties. Earlier this year, Heskey became caught up in a legal dispute surrounding an allegedly fraudulent £15m takeover of Cypriot club Apollon Limassol by British businessman Craig Gabriel.

Heskey had been lined up to become the face of the takeover and a club director. There is no suggestion of wrongdoing on his part.

In 2023, Heskey was found to have defaulted on £92,000 in tax relating to his work as a football development officer between 2017 and 2020. He was handed a £42,000 penalty.

That same year, a celebrity bar and restaurant he had funded, and which was overseen by his wife Chantelle, was wound up by the courts with debts totalling £163,000.

Former England footballer Heskey has found love with former Miss Blackpool Slusarczyk

Parea, which opened in 2018, had been a regular haunt of footballers and television personalities, including members of the Real Housewives of Cheshire cast. But a local catering company applied to have the business wound up over unpaid debts.

The restaurant had previously made headlines in 2019 when its first anniversary party featured sushi served on a semi-naked woman lying on a table, her modesty largely preserved by strategically placed leaves and pieces of salmon.

In 2024, Heskey faced further financial difficulties linked to his involvement in a celebrity investment scheme that became embroiled in a £1.6billion tax dispute.

The scheme was reportedly operated by Ingenious Media, a financing company that backed dozens of films. Investors were said to include Beckham, Gerrard, Jeremy Paxman, Robbie Williams and Heskey, with a minimum investment of £50,000.

Gerrard and the composer Andrew Lloyd Webber were among those who launched legal proceedings against HSBC in 2018, alleging that the bank had ‘dishonestly assisted’ Ingenious Media.

In the same year, Heskey was ordered to pay almost £200,000 in a dispute involving an unpaid £1.63m tax bill.

His personal life has also become complicated. Heskey appears to be estranged from his wife Chantelle, whom he married in 2014 and with whom he has four children. In August, she branded him ‘vile’ following a holiday he took with his new partner.

Heskey had gone public with his relationship with Jade Slusarczyk, a former Sky Sports walk-on girl accompanying darts players to the oche, in July. Within a month, the couple were holidaying in Cyprus and Greece, sharing photographs of their trip on Instagram.

Parea, a popular Cheshire bar loved by footballers and celebrities and owned by Heskey and his wife, was wound up with debts of £163,000

‘The best two weeks away with you,’ he wrote. The posts provoked an angry response from Chantelle, who has begun divorce proceedings and accused Heskey of letting his family down in comments beneath the photographs. She subsequently claimed that Heskey had deleted her comment and described him as ‘vile’.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted Mrs Heskey's representatives on multiple occasions, but they have declined to comment.

Emile and Chantelle have two sons, Reigan and Jaden, both footballers, and two younger daughters, Milanna and Mendez. Jaden made his Manchester City debut in the Carabao Cup last season and is now on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, while Reigan was sold to Cologne in the summer.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport last year, Heskey praised his sons' athletic ability and suggested that both could one day play for England's senior team. He was happy to talk on that occasion, speaking as he helped coach children at a football camp.

This time, however, Daily Mail Sport has been met with silence. We have made repeated attempts, through multiple reporters, to put questions to Heskey about his involvement with Supreme CBD. His representatives have either declined to comment or failed to respond.

We wanted to know whether he was aware of the advertising rulings against Supreme CBD, and whether he had any concerns about the medical claims made by its founder. We would also have welcomed his account of the personal and financial difficulties described here.

And so we are left watching Heskey from afar, returning to the warehouse for video after video, smiling and cracking jokes with Fowler.

Heskey scores the fifth goal in England's 5-1 trouncing of Germany in 2001

We have made repeated attempts to put questions to Heskey about his involvement with Supreme CBD. His representatives have either declined to comment or failed to respond

‘When you find the best dose for you, there's no going back,’ he declares in the caption to one post from October.

Perched on a green sofa, encouraging his followers to buy products from a company with a deeply controversial advertising record, he seems entirely at ease.

Whether Heskey has any reservations about the business whose products he so enthusiastically promotes is something we would dearly like to know.

For now, the former England striker is still smiling for the camera.

#964. 'My job combines my passion for gaming and football'

Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

We're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

Growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

So a typical day for us, we'll get a new build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

So even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save."

So as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

So I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a new job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

One of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

Working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

#963. Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows

Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," said the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons."

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

The study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters said. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%."

It is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

While the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

And even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

#961. Why Oliver Glasner is taking on the Nottingham Forest dressing room: The frustrations behind 'English-speakers' rant, key players up for sale in January, his tick-list for transfer targets and the Morgan Gibbs-White conundrum

Published: 12:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 12:00 EST, 26 November 2026

Nottingham Forest's restless players have already seen off two managers in the past 12 months but now Oliver Glasner believes he will beat them at their own game.

The strength of feeling within the squad helped force Ange Postecoglou and Sean Dyche out of the door after 39 and 114 days respectively and after a dodgy start to his reign, there were probably one or two who thought Glasner would go the same way.

No Premier League boss is ever immune to results and another run of defeats would make Glasner vulnerable. Forest have won two games all season and are above the relegation zone only on goal difference, ahead of Friday night’s clash with Chelsea at the City Ground.

But as things stand, Glasner has the backing of Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis to make the changes he needs – and that could be bad news for some senior players.

Daily Mail Sport examines the power struggle bubbling away at the City Ground...

Nottingham Forest's restless players have already seen off two managers in the past 12 months but now Oliver Glasner believes he will beat them at their own game

Glasner took aim at some players' lack of English skills in light of a disappointing start to the season that sees his side hovering outside the relegation zone on goal difference alone

Early in his reign, Mikel Arteta stamped his authority on Arsenal, moving on high-profile players like Mesut Ozil, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Alexandre Lacazette.

Even at the start of his managerial career, Arteta would not compromise and was prepared to clash with big names if they would not match his standards. Arteta knew what he wanted and if he had to fight some stars to get it, all well and good. Now look where Arsenal are today.

It will not have escaped Glasner that despite their success, the champions work ferociously hard and seem to carry no outsized egos or sense of entitlement. That may worry certain Forest players.

This is the source of Glasner’s remarks about players not learning English – but that is not his only issue with the squad. He wants time-keeping to be sharper, training sessions to be slicker.

It is thought Forest will listen to offers for Ola Aina and Callum Hudson-Odoi in January, while Ibrahim Sangare has work to do to force his way into Glasner’s plans. Hudson-Odoi and Aina are influential figures in the dressing room and Sangare is highly respected, too. Is Glasner trying to smash this power base in order to cement his own?

Glasner wants to add more athleticism and physicality to his squad in January as he has been alarmed at how Forest have been outmuscled in certain games. As things stand, he has the mandate to shape things his way after a three-hour meeting with Marinakis in London this week.

It will not be easy. Glasner can change some things yet a fair number of this squad are on their fifth manager. They were outstanding for a season under Nuno Espirito Santo in 2024-25 but they have drifted since. It still feels a long way until January and that is why – more than ever – Glasner needs the captain on board...

Glasner wants players' time-keeping to be sharper and training sessions to be slicker

It is thought Forest will listen to offers for influential full back Ola Aina in January

A glance at the numbers shows that Morgan Gibbs-White is having an outstanding season. He has created the second-most big chances of any player, the third-most chances from open play, and is in the top three for 'expected assists' too. Not bad for a player in a team above the relegation zone thanks only to goal difference.

Albeit from a smaller sample size, Gibbs-White is performing better than last term on all of these metrics (per 90 minutes). Last season, he finished with 15 league goals and four assists. England boss Thomas Tuchel appreciates the underlying numbers and after leaving Gibbs-White out of his World Cup squad, has brought him back into the fold this autumn.

Gibbs-White is Forest’s most talented player and it is believed he would have accepted a move away from the club last summer, after watching Elliot Anderson join Manchester City.

There was tentative interest from Chelsea but Gibbs-White wanted to play in the Champions League and it is thought he would have been open to a move to Manchester United. The 26-year-old’s boyhood idol was Wayne Rooney – but the Old Trafford club have never truly pushed for him. That may change if Bruno Fernandes leaves next summer.

Gibbs-White is the highest-paid player in Forest's history and is halfway through a three-year deal. Few expect him to be at the club for life and if he moves in summer 2027, nobody will be surprised.

Yet there is a feeling in the game that Gibbs-White’s body language can count against him at times. When team-mates are not quite on his wavelength, Gibbs-White is often quick to show his frustration. If he creates a chance that a colleague misses, it is a similar story.

Morgan Gibbs-White's numbers are very impressive this season. At times, the same can't be said for his body language

It is difficult to be rational in the heat of battle but could Gibbs-White try to stop these issues at source? At Forest, each part of the team – defenders, midfielders and forwards – have discussions before matches. That would be the perfect opportunity for Gibbs-White to guide others, to explain his thinking and where they should be when he has the ball in certain areas.

Because unless the player is Diego Maradona or Lionel Messi, top clubs do not look at talent alone before making signings. Gibbs-White has the tools to play for an elite team but in other aspects, there may still be some work to do.

Glasner and his staff hope Forest’s best player can inspire others, as he has in the past. Club skipper Ryan Yates returned to the starting XI for the last two matches and if he loses his place against Chelsea, Gibbs-White would logically regain the armband. How Forest need a captain’s performance from him against Xabi Alonso’s faltering side.

Abhinand Lal is in the Institute for Integrative Biology of the Cell (I2BC), French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA), French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), Paris-Saclay University, 91190 Gif-sur-Yvette, France.

Daan Noordermeer is in the Institute for Integrative Biology of the Cell (I2BC), French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA), French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), Paris-Saclay University, 91190 Gif-sur-Yvette, France.

Large regions of chromosomes are organized into a state known as heterochromatin. This densely packed form of DNA represses gene activity. Curiously, some families of clustered genes can be activated even though they are packed as heterochromatin. Writing in Nature, Buckley et al.1 report findings that explain this paradox: they show how opposing mechanisms that control the organization of heterochromatin promote the stochastic activation of genes in the protocadherin (Pcdh) gene cluster, thereby supporting proper nervous-system development.

#959. Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).

The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.

"In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," said Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president. "You could have a severe vitamin D deficiency for months before any symptoms appear at all. The same applies for vitamin B12. By the time symptoms appear, such as nerve damage, it's already too late."

A long-term B12 deficiency can damage the spinal cord, leading to numbness in the limbs, muscle weakness or even paralysis. Less common deficiency-related brain damage can cause memory loss and mental health issues.

All B vitamins play an important role in metabolism, blood formation and healthy nerve function.

Vitamins, along with various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, iron, iodine and zinc, are classed as micronutrients. The body needs to source them from food, as it cannot produce them itself. Our bodies also need macronutrients like carbohydrates, carbohydrates, protein and fats that provide us with energy.

If the body consumes less food than it needs to maintain all bodily functions over a prolonged period of time, then this is known as undernutrition. A recent World Food Organization (FAO) report estimates that approximately 645 million people worldwide suffer from chronic undernutrition.

Malnutrition, on the other hand, occurs when we consume enough calories but lack certain macronutrients or micronutrients in our food. This, too, can make one sick over time and even prove fatal. About 2 billion people worldwide suffer from this so-called hidden hunger, most of them in the Global South. That said, even some people in industrialized nations lack important micronutrients in their nutrition.

One study, for instance, found that just under three-quarters of the US population did not meet the recommended daily intake of vitamin D between 2007 and 2010, with more than two-thirds falling short of the recommended amount of vitamin E. And in Germany, about one-third of the population suffered from vitamin D deficiency in 2017, according to the German Nutrition Society. Such deficiency can cause bone, joint and muscle pain. It may also lead to an increased risk of falls and bone fractures.

About one-third of Germans also had an insufficient intake of iodine, a trace element that is indispensable for the production of thyroid hormones. Iodine deficiency can therefore disrupt normal thyroid function. Not only that — during pregnancy, a baby's brain and nervous system can only properly develop with an adequate supply of iodine.

The cultivation of agricultural produce with partially long shelf life or high yields has in some cases caused a decrease in the micronutrient content of fruits, vegetables and grains. Whether this drop in micronutrients is impacting human health, however, is a matter of debate.

Malnutrition can result from an unbalanced diet that, while filling and providing energy, lacks essential micronutrients. Examples of such empty calories include fast food and highly processed foods, as well as white bread and white rice.

Poverty is often the reason for such an unbalanced diet, for example when people in the Global South can only afford to buy staples such as flour or rice.

Another study found that in Germany, households at risk of poverty are more likely to consume foods that are low in nutrients and high in calories.

Depression is also associated with an increased risk of nutrient deficiency. "People often lose their appetite, and when they neglect their self-care, they may end up eating a very unbalanced diet," Pirlich told DW. His research shows that older adults and people who live alone often develop malnutrition, too. The risk also increases the more medications a person takes.

Many diseases result in the body being less efficient at absorbing or utilizing nutrients through the intestines. This applies to people with inflammatory or chronic disease, such as Crohn's disease, celiac disease, liver disease and cancer.

The DGEM estimates that some 30% of all patients receiving inpatient care in Germany are affected by or at risk of malnutrition. Yet health insurance data shows that only about 1% of patients are screened and treated for nutrient deficiencies.

Often, patients' malnutrition worsens during their hospital stay. The consequences can be serious, potentially causing additional complications, delayed recuperation, longer hospital stays and even increased mortality rates. This results in higher healthcare expenditure, amounting to billions each year.

German policymakers and medical associations are therefore developing a plan to better screen for and treat malnutrition in hospitals. The road map will be ready by 2027 and copy the Dutch approach in the sense that all patients are checked for nutritional deficiencies upon hospital admission.

Pirlich wants to see such screenings for at-risk groups in outpatient clinics, too: "This includes all those with chronic and serious illnesses and, above all, older adults."

To prevent poverty-related malnutrition, Pirlich suggests increased access to healthy food, offering free school meals as an example.

The nutritional expert recommends eating a diet that is varied and largely plant-based. "Secondary plant compounds have a very positive effect, and if you eat a highly diverse diet, you consume many different foods that are [nutritionally] beneficial," said Pirlich.

There's a simple rule of thumb: The more colorful your food, the better.

Also, cook vegetables as gently as possible, because overheating and keeping them warm for too long destroys their vitamins. Long storage periods also lead to vitamin loss, so it makes sense to go for seasonal and regional foods in particular.

But even when ensuring a healthy and balanced diet, some people still develop a nutrient deficiency. A blood test can provide clarity, and dietary supplements may help make up for the deficiency.

This article was originally written in German.

#958. Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds

There are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

“I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

“The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible plan or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

Alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

The Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

It is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

Noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ

“I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, said. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”

John Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

Alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

Frank’s start to life at Palace begins with defeat but an improved display. Coventry are up to 13th with their fourth win of the season.

Another home win for Tottenham, who managed the game well and introduced a new star to the Premier League in Williams-Barnett

What a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Bournemouth make it nine wins in a row in all competitions after doing enough in the first half to get the job done.

Leeds finish the match in style as Aaronson puts the seal on an impressive away day.

It’s all over and Sunderland deservedly leave with a point. Villa will be very disappointed by their display.

What was I saying in the last post?! The home side are on the attack Thomas-Asante pokes a shot at goal and forces Henderson into a save but hits his own player McNeil, who bundles the ball in the net.

Can Chelsea stage a late fightback? Will we get a winner between Coventry and Palace?

Needing a goal, Emery makes a bold decision to take off Villa’s top scorer and bring on Madjo.

Despite the two-goal lead and the magnificent debut performance of Luca Williams-Barnett, the home support has remained subdued throughout the afternoon.

At times, the shouts of two children sat just behind the press box feel like by far the loudest noise in the stadium - although that might just be proximity.

Much quieter half at the CBS Arena but Palace are more likely to get a third goal.

This has gone from bad to worse for Chelsea. One supporter near the dug-outs was so angry at Leeds scoring a third goal that he got up and screamed his displeasure at manager Xabi Alonso.

1999 was the last time Leeds won at Chelsea. Today looks like they will get another, as Okafor takes advantage of more poor defending to finish past Martinez.

Villa’s fans are now chanting loudly for substitute John McGinn to be introduced.

They are getting their wish, too, as the Scotland international is coming on with winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

Morgan Rogers and Chelsea are pretty upset about that penalty being awarded to Leeds. They felt the ball struck him too far up his arm to be a penalty. Calvert-Lewin took his spot-kick superbly and it’s gone very, very quiet among the home fans.

Everything Luca Williams-Barnett touches is turning to gold today. He has a goal to his name already, and adds an assist just six minutes into the second half.

From almost the halfway line, he drove forward, weaving his way expertly into the box before picking out Dominic Solanke in the middle of the box, who tapped the ball into the back of the net.

However, the atmosphere is still a touch subdued, despite James Maddison urging the crowd to make themselves heard almost immediately after the goal, the noise drops to almost a murmur.

Rogers blocks Bogle’s drive with his arm and Michael Oliver gives a penalty to Leeds. After a long check, VAR confirms it.

Calvert-Lewin steps up and sends Martinez the wrong way. The away team deserves this. They have been the better side. That is Calvert-Lewin’s 100th club career goal.

Williams-Barnet gets one-on-one with Furlong and gets past him with ease before firing a cross for Solanke to finish.

The whistle blows for the second half around the grounds. What will the second 45 minutes have for us?

A real lack of quality here from both teams, and Sunderland deserve credit for weathering the early pressure.

Villa appear short of creativity and have managed only one shot on target in the first-half.

Sunderland have defended resolutely and caused Villa’s back-four some problems in the rare moments they have attacked.

Unai Emery marched into the dressing room after the half-time whistle and has much to ponder.

Some boos from the Chelsea fans at half-time. Calvert-Lewin could have had a hat-trick in that first half, sending one header against the bar, two too close to Martinez and flicking a shot just wide. Leeds also had a goal ruled out for offside.

Chelsea just stopped playing after taking the lead.

That half was all about Luca Williams-Barnett. The 18-year-old scored in his first start, and had two opportunities to add to his tally just before the break. He had a header tipped over the bar by Christian Walton and a chance from close range stopped on the line. The future looks bright, as they say.

However, Tottenham faded after a strong opening 15 minutes, and Ipswich were able to break up play and get forward more, exploiting the home side’s lack of a defensive midfielder, and that will be something for Roberto De Zerbi to address in the break.

We have whistles around the ground. That was breathless stuff.

The visitors will feel they should be in front at the break. First, Muharemovic thinks he has scored when he head in a cross from Justin but he was offside.

Then Ampadu’s long throw finds Calvert-Lewin in space and his shot is saved by Martinez. Should have done better there.

Bournemouth finish the half in style. Kluivert gets the second when he taps in a cross from Tavernier.

Palace hit back again. Pino clips a cross to Larsen at the far post and he heads past Rushworth coolly.

Courtesy of Opta: Aged 18 years and 51 days, Luca Williams-Barnett is Tottenham Hotspur’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

Villa are in desperate need of a spark and one has to wonder when John McGinn will be introduced. McGinn is on the bench today and the home team are crying out for some inspiration.

Villa did start brilliantly, yet the game has now petered out into a mess of misplaced passes and poor decision-making.

Still no clean sheet for Emi Martinez. But Noah Okafor’s goal wasn’t his fault – he was let down by some bad defending from Wesley Fofana and Josh Acheampong.

Martinez did start Chelsea’s 2-0 victory over Everton, but he didn’t last the full game as he had to be replaced because of injury.

A touch of Hollywood royalty in attendance at Tottenham on this cold November afternoon with Sir Kenneth Branagh and Ryan Reynolds in attendance.

Reynolds is a co-owner of Wrexham, who are currently playing in the Championship at Lincoln City, but he has chosen to watch football in north London instead.

Sakamoto puts Palace back in front with a brilliant finish. Rudoni gets away from Khalaili and crosses to the Japan international. Sakamoto brings it down nicely then rifles a shot into the top corner.

That lead did not last long for Chelsea. The away side hit back within three minutes as Okafor shoots through the legs of Colwill and into the net.

Another full debutant and another goal. This time at Stamford Bridge as Emegha latches onto a ball from Rogers and blasts an unstoppable shot from distance.

Emegha had to wait a while to make his first start for Chelsea, but he’s marked it with a really well taken goal. Leeds will be disappointed with the time and space he and Morgan Rogers, who provided the assist, were given, but it was a good finish.

Caicedo just can’t get going this season. That back injury that forced him off the pitch for a minute earlier has now resulted in him having to be replaced by Jordan Henderson. That’s a real blow to Alonso and Chelsea.

Villa were completely dominant in the opening ten minutes but Sunderland have now managed to subdue the home team.

Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson are both impressing for the home team. Villa do appear a little vulnerable in defence when Sunderland do break forward.

Today will be a day that 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett will not forget in a hurry, he has been energetic since the start and marked his maiden Premier League start with an early goal.

The actual goal might have been a tap-in, but it has injected life into the crowd who had otherwise been largely subdued from the start.

Confusion on the touchline for Chelsea. Caicedo was down after hurting his back. Alonso tried to stop his phyisos going straight on to the pitch, but referee Michael Oliver called them on. That meant Caicedo had to spend a minute off the pitch under the latest rules.

Remember this moment because on his first senior start Williams-Barnet has made it a special one with goal. It was scrappy but he will not care. The Tottenham fans have been talking about his young fan for a long time.

Equaliser for Palace and Frank. Very good response from his players as Larsen flicks the ball to Pino and the Spain international fires into the net.

No shots on target from either side but it is already shaping up to be attack vs defence. Villa are dominating the goal and looking threatening.

Awoniyi is through one-on-one with Henderson, goes around the keeper but Disasi does brilliantly to recover and make the block.

Worst possible start for Frank and Palace as Awoniyi gets his second goal of the season with a cool finish.

A video of De Zerbi saying “let’s go” in a manner that might be more at home in American Football is shown before the teams come out onto the pitch.

The atmosphere feels a bit subdued so far, but it is an important match for Tottenham.

This is probably the kiss of death from me, but I’m really looking forward to watching Tarik Muharemovic today. The defender has impressed me every time I’ve watched Leeds on television this season and looks to be one of the signings of the summer. Dare I say it, but Chelsea could have done worse than sign him given their troubles at the back. Emi Martinez is back in goal for the home side. He’s yet to keep a clean sheet since signing from Aston Villa.

Thomas Frank declared “it’s good to be back in the circus” of football management ahead of his first match as Crystal Palace boss.

The 53-year-old Dane admitted he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, “eating too well” and collecting passport stamps, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a new job and she told him, “(It’s) because you can’t help yourself”.

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal, but for now he has a team to rescue from a relegation fight, beginning with today’s trip to Coventry.

If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better.

Of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I’ve learned, definitely.

I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

Construction news: work on the North Stand behind one of the Villa Park goals continues to progress.

There are clear structural changes since Villa’s last home game and a mural of fans makes it more appealing to look at.

This stand is scheduled to be ready for next season and will increase Villa’s capacity to over 50,000.

Tottenham’s impressive run of form came to a crashing halt with a 1-0 defeat to Leeds just before the international break, but manager Roberto De Zerbi will be hoping for a fresh start - even if he will not be pitchside after picking up a second yellow card of the season.

De Zerbi made six changes from the aforementioned defeat to Leeds, including a first start for teenager Luca Williams-Barnett, a player who has come through the club’s academy.

There is no place in the squad for Sandro Tonali or Tosin Adarabioyo, but James Maddison will start for the first time since the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea in October.

Aston Villa 2.0 was always likely to be a slow-burner, and it is proving exactly that for Unai Emery.

His team has impressed and underwhelmed in equal measure so far this season but this is an opportunity to hoist themselves up the table.

A clean sheet would be a good starting point, as they have not secured a shutout in front of their own fans in the league since March.

There is no Alejandro Garnacho or Tammy Abraham in the matchday squad today.

Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

#957. Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 17 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

For players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards)

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards)

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension)

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension)

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension)

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension)

Leny Yoro - Manchester United (red card suspension)

James Tarkowski - Everton (red card suspension)
